validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: STRONGLY CONFIRMED, well outside GEM-only territory -- this is a real, bilaterally-negotiated cross-border pipeline with a paper trail on both the Kazakh and Chinese sides. Directly read the underlying interstate instrument, https://adilet.zan.kz/eng/docs/P1300000277 (Decree of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan No.277, March 27, 2013, approving an agreement signed December 8, 2012 in Astana between Kazakhstan and China): Article 1 names the pipeline 'Sarybulak-Zimunay', connecting Sarybulak gas field (East Kazakhstan Region) to the town of Zimunay in Xinjiang via the Maikapchagay border point, with a stated 'transfer capability of 500 million cubic meters per year'; Article 2 names the responsible organizations verbatim as 'Tarbagatay Munay' LLP (Kazakh side) and 'Xinjiang Guanhei Zimunai LNG Development Limited Liability Company' (Chinese side) -- an EXACT match to GEM's Owner1/Owner2. Independently, Xinhua's wire report via people.com.cn (April 3, 2014; live copy dead/stub-redirects now, but fully readable via Wayback: https://web.archive.org/web/20220120124150/http://russian.people.com.cn/31518/8588901.html) describes the SAME pipeline operated by 'Xinjiang energy company Guanhui' and 'Kazakhstan's Tarbagatai Munai', states it is China's first privately-run cross-border gas pipeline, that construction began May 2011 and it was 'officially commissioned June 20, 2013', and that by March 27, 2014 over 300 million m3 had already been delivered to China -- i.e. gas was demonstrably flowing. A third independent source, nangs.org (May 24, 2022, quoting Kazakhstan's Energy Minister B. Akchulakov) confirms the December 2012 agreement, the June 2013 commissioning, the 50/50 domestic-Kazakhstan/export-to-China split of Sarybulak gas, and reports the pipeline still moving gas as of 2022 (~4 of a planned 75 million m3 delivered to China by May 2022, export TEMPORARILY paused from Jan 1 2022 over local Zaisan-district residents' concerns about field depletion -- not a shutdown of the line itself, and domestic supply continued). A fourth independent source, RFE/RL's Kazakh service (rus.azattyq.org / azattyqasia.org, April 25, 2024) confirms the Sarybulak field has been in continuous production in Zaisan district since 2013, >10 years on. So Status=operating is corroborated by evidence spanning 2014-2024, not just a stale approval decree. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- both the treaty and Kazakhstan's Order No.350 (General Gasification Scheme 2023-2030, https://adilet.zan.kz/rus/docs/G23JVM00350, para 95, verified live) call it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/main gas pipeline), matching GEM's PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 39-row Kazakhstan-gas roster -- no other row shares this name, these endpoints (Sarybulak Gas Field -> Zimunay/Xinjiang), or this China-crossing geometry; this is a genuinely distinct, non-duplicated entity. FuelSource=Sarybulak Gas Field and the Location block (StartLocation/StartState-Province=East Kazakhstan/StartCountryOrArea=Kazakhstan, EndLocation=Zimunay/EndState-Province=Xinjiang/EndCountryOrArea=China) are all directly confirmed verbatim by the treaty text (Article 1) -- high confidence, no changes needed.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC -- Length. I independently fetched and read Kazakhstan's Order of the Minister of Energy No.350 (adilet.zan.kz/rus/docs/G23JVM00350) directly, paragraph 95: 'На территории Восточно-Казахстанской области реализован проект строительства магистрального газопровода "Сарыбулак – Зимунай" в направлении Китайской Народной Республики обшей протяженностью 92,5 км' (a project to build the 'Sarybulak-Zimunay' trunk gas pipeline toward the PRC, total length 92.5 km, has been implemented in East Kazakhstan region) -- this is an EXACT match to GEM's LengthKnown=92.50 km, from the sheet's own already-cited ref. HOWEVER, Xinhua's 2014 wire (via people.com.cn, read via the Wayback copy above) independently states: 'Его общая протяженность составляет 110 км' (its total length is 110 km) -- a ~19% disagreement on the same 'total length' framing. This is exactly the discrepancy GEM's own wiki article body (not carried into the sheet's ResearcherNotes) already flags: 'The length of the pipeline is reported to be 92.5 km in the official Kazakh documents, whereas the Chinese media report the total length of 110 km, including a 25 km long segment within China' (citing gas.in-en.com, which I could not independently re-verify live -- HTTP 403 on direct fetch, no Wayback snapshot found, so I am relying on the wiki's own paraphrase, not citing it myself). If that 25 km China-side figure is right, the implied Kazakh-side length is ~85 km, which is only ~8% off Order 350's 92.5 km -- plausibly the same underlying route measured from slightly different start/border points, not a fabricated or erroneous value on either side. I am not recommending a value change (GEM's number matches its own government-source ref exactly), but per the >10%-disagreement standing rule this is a genuine, documented spec caveat that belongs in ResearcherNotes rather than staying silent. Diameter: currently blank on both the sheet and gem.wiki's own infobox; I found no source (treaty, Order 350, Xinhua, nangs.org, azattyq) stating a diameter value anywhere -- leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate.

I fetched the live page directly: it is the 'H2 Infrastructure Map Europe' WordPress site (European hydrogen pipeline mapping project) -- I grepped the full HTML for 'Kazakh', 'Sarybulak', and 'Zimunay' and found none of the three anywhere on the page. This ref does not, and structurally cannot, support a claim about a Kazakhstan-China gas pipeline; it passed the worklist's automated liveness check (200 OK) but that check never tested for topical relevance. The underlying VALUE (transmission) is very likely correct regardless -- both the interstate treaty and Order 350 describe this as a dedicated trunk/main line carrying gas from a single field to a single cross-border delivery point, the textbook shape of a transmission pipeline, not a gathering/feeder line -- so this is a citation-integrity defect, not a misclassification of the pipeline itself.

summary: P6787 Sarybulak-Zimunay: existence/classification/duplicate all CONFIRMED via the Kazakh-China interstate treaty (P1300000277), Order 350, Xinhua/people.com.cn (2014), nangs.org (2022) and Azattyq (2024) -- a real, well-documented cross-border trunk line, capacity 0.5 bcm/y and owners exactly matched by the treaty text. Two ref-quality caveats staged: PipelineType's h2inframap.eu citation is topically unrelated (swap to Order 350) and Owner's people.com.cn link now stub-redirects (add its Wayback copy). One spec caveat: GEM's Length=92.5km matches Order 350 exactly, but Xinhua reports a 110km 'total length' for the full cross-border corridor -- plausible Kazakh-side-only vs whole-corridor scoping, not treated as an error, but recommended for a ResearcherNotes line. Diameter remains UNRESOLVED (blank everywhere, no source found).
